history.period: Claimed 1703 (tantrik Udaynarayan Brahmachari); present structure often dated 1803 (Shankar Ghosh) — conflicting
history.summary: One of Kolkata's oldest Kali temples, on Bidhan Sarani near College Street, North Kolkata; identity confirmed. Tradition: tantrik Udaynarayan Brahmachari hand-built a clay Kali idol in a dense jungle (Sutanuti-Gobindapur area) in 1703; a marble plaque credits Shankar Ghosh as the 1803 founder (founding-date conflict — verify). The name is locally said to come from 'than-than', the bell rung to warn of dacoits in the forest. The presiding deity Siddheshwari ('wish-fulfiller') is considered 'jagrat' (awakened); the clay idol is remade and painted red and black yearly. Intimately tied to Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa, who visited often, sang to the goddess, and whose words 'Shankarer hridoy majhe, Kali biraje' are engraved on the wall; the non-veg prasad (dab-chingri) tradition traces to his offering for Keshab Chandra Sen's recovery, and daab-and-chini is also offered. Founder Shankar Ghosh's grandson Subodh Chandra Ghosh (Swami Subodhananda) was a direct disciple of Ramakrishna. Tantric temple; Tuesdays and Saturdays are most auspicious. Wikipedia notes animal sacrifice continues on amavasya nights and Kali Puja (unverified — verify).

name: Thanthania Kalibari Temple
town_description: Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal, is a major metropolis on the Hooghly river — India's cultural capital, famous for its intense Kali worship centered on Kalighat and Dakshineswar as well as historic Kalibaris like Thanthania.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU), roughly 17 km away.
travel.railway: Sealdah station, about 3 km away; nearest metro MG Road.
travel.road: Bidhan Sarani at Rajendra Deb Lane crossing, near College Street Market, North Kolkata; best reached by taxi/auto or metro to MG Road.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Kali Puja (Kartik Amavasya) draws the biggest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Wikipedia reports 6 AM-11 AM and 3 PM-8 PM daily; other listings say 7 AM-12:30 PM and 3:30-10 PM (conflicting — verify).
